measurement.name: Antarctic Slope Current
measurement.range_interpretation: Reported jet narrower than 28 km in one dated snapshot; not a 28 km point, zero-to-28 interval, confidence bound, whole-current envelope or annual range.
measurement.geographic_scope: Riiser-Larsenisen continental shelf/slope, southeastern Weddell Sea; section 2 offshore narrow jet embedded in broader southwestward flow. No exact paired geographic width limits supplied.
measurement.section_orientation: Cross-shelf/slope section context; no exact paired width endpoints or flow-normal orientation diagnosed by OSW.
measurement.layer: Detided LADCP horizontal-current context at 100 m (paragraph 5 and Figure 1). Surface-intensified jet; no uniform vertical width slab inferred. 3000 m isobath describes bottom topography.
measurement.time_convention: One observed section on 23 February 2009; January 31 is separate. Neither the 2010 publication date nor the M6 2017–2021 record dates this jet.
measurement.boundary_rule: Author reports jet narrower than 28 km. Velocity cutoff and paired edges unresolved; peak 28 cm/s and broader-flow speed about 10 cm/s are not boundary thresholds.
measurement.source_citation: Chavanne, C.P., K.J. Heywood, K.W. Nicholls and I. Fer (2010), Observations of the Antarctic Slope Undercurrent in the southeastern Weddell Sea, Geophysical Research Letters 37, L13601, doi:10.1029/2010GL043603.
measurement.source_locator: Primary publisher indexed text: section 2 Observations paragraph 5; processing paragraph 4; Figure 1/2 captions establish section dates and 100 m horizontal-current context.
measurement.extraction_method: Reported qualifier, reference scale and date transcribed from primary publisher indexed body/captions; original PDF/pixels and fields not acquired or digitized.
measurement.source_quality_note: Primary publisher indexed passages/captions reviewed. Original PDF, figure pixels, fields and paired width edges unavailable. Width constraint describes a narrow jet within broader flow, not complete ASC width.
remaining_gates: Acquire original paper/figures and paired width boundary method.
Recover compatible repeated sections before seasonal widths or annual extrema.

original_regional_context.processing_context: LADCP LDEO IX.5; least-squares M2 tidal removal from depth-averaged currents; source-reported, not reproduced by OSW.
original_regional_context.display_aria_label: Antarctic Slope Current narrow jet: source reports less than 28 km on 23 February 2009, in 100 m detided LADCP context. No point width, lower bound, zero-to-28 interval, confidence guarantee or full-current envelope.
original_regional_context.display_caption: Source reports a narrow southwestward jet <28 km on 23 February 2009, within broader slower southwestward flow. Representative width, lower bound and numeric uncertainty remain unknown.
original_regional_context.display_method_note: Primary publisher indexed text/captions reviewed; original PDF and figure pixels unavailable. 100 m is the horizontal-current context; 3000 m is bottom topography. Peak 28 cm/s and background about 10 cm/s are not width cutoffs. No annual range or mapped width band.

previous_source_review_record.reason: M6 local velocity measurements and the inspected 2017–2021 study do not supply paired current-width boundaries. Mooring spacing and dynamical length scales cannot be admitted as current width.

evidence.citation: Darelius, Fer, Janout, Daae and Steiger (2024), Observations of the Antarctic Slope Current in the Southeastern Weddell Sea: A Bottom-Enhanced Current and Its Seasonal Variability, JGR Oceans 129, e2023JC020666.
evidence.locator: Original PDF pp3–4, Table 1 and section 2.1; p13, section 4.
evidence.supports: 5 km is M530–M740 spacing; 80 km separates M2570 and M740. L=10 km is a dynamical scale selected with reference to a trough corner; later 10 km is a radius-of-curvature estimate. None is current width.

evidence.citation: Darelius, Janout, Fer and Sallée (2024), PANGAEA.964717, CC BY 4.0.
evidence.locator: Dataset parameter list, coverage and released nominal 228 m ADCP bin.
evidence.supports: Geographic velocity at one fixed station and depth supplies no lateral current edges or annual width range.
